understanding.purpose: Provide an inventory of servers and highlight operational issues.
understanding.reading: Readers scan hosts and roles, compare zones and CPU counts, then check status and read notes for exceptions. The long note determines the height of its row and can absorb wrapping.
groups: Host and Role identify each server and its function.
Zone and CPU describe placement and capacity.
Status and Notes pair the operational state with its explanation.
may_wrap: The long Notes entry can wrap at word boundaries.
Zone identifiers can wrap at hyphens if more space is needed for Notes.

preferred.name: r0A
preferred.note: Keep the inventory fields on one line and give the remaining width to the exceptional note.

acceptable.name: r0C
acceptable.note: Give the frequently scanned inventory fields more breathing room and accept a taller note row.

bad.name: r0B
bad.note: Allow zone identifiers to wrap at hyphens to give the long note more room.
bad.why: Every zone identifier wraps, making the routine rows taller and harder to scan for the sake of one fewer line in the exceptional note.

rationale: r0A keeps the host, role, zone, CPU, and status values on single lines while giving the exceptional note enough width to remain readable. The six short rows retain a compact, consistent rhythm, and the tall row is visibly associated with the one server that needs explanation. r0C also preserves the identifiers but spends more width on already short fields, making the note taller.

general: Keep repeated identifiers intact when wrapping would disrupt scanning across many rows.
Allocate width according to content and reading role; an occasional long note need not dictate the height of every row.
specific: The zone values need about 90px including padding to stay on one line.
Only one server has a substantive note, so its taller row is a reasonable exception.

tradeoffs: A wider Notes column shortens the exceptional row, but taking that width from Zone makes every zone value wrap. r0C gives the short fields more breathing room at the cost of a longer note.
uncertain: The ranges are approximate and should be treated as individual adjustments, not combined endpoints; widths must still total at most 633px. The exact point at which a small change in Notes width alters its line breaks would need another browser render.

critique.good: Host, role, zone, CPU and status values remain intact, making the ordinary rows compact and easy to compare. The notes column has enough width to keep the exception readable without splitting words.
critique.problems: The long note makes its row much taller than the others and leaves substantial empty space in the neighboring cells.
critique.cause: The 263px Notes column wraps the exceptional entry into six lines. The other columns are already at the stated widths needed to keep their contents on one line, so giving Notes more space would compromise those values.

critique.good: The 283px Notes column reduces the exceptional note to five lines and gives it a comfortable reading width. Host, role, CPU and status values remain intact.
critique.problems: Every zone identifier wraps, making all ordinary rows taller and interrupting comparisons down the Zone column. The additional height outweighs the space saved in the exception row.
critique.cause: At 70px, Zone has only 49px for text, less than the 69px needed for a one-line identifier. The 20px transferred to Notes is taken from a column repeated in every row.

critique.good: The identification and operational columns have generous breathing room, and their values stay on one line. The table remains easy to scan across ordinary rows.
critique.problems: The note becomes a narrow seven-line block, making the exception row taller and increasing the empty space beside it. The extra width in the short-value columns provides little additional benefit.
critique.cause: Host, Role, Zone, CPU and Status receive more width than their one-line contents require, leaving only 213px for Notes.

review.method: two fresh-context blind reviews; letters shuffled; includes browser auto layout and equal widths as neutral references

r0B.why: The note has a readable measure, but every zone identifier wraps, making routine rows taller and harder to scan.

ref_equal.why: The narrow Notes column turns the incident into a long stack of short lines, creating an exceptionally tall row and separating the surrounding records.

ref_auto.why: The note reads well, but zone identifiers break across three lines and some host names split, disrupting identification and row scanning.

r0A.why: Host names and zones stay intact, compact fields are sized to their content, and the note has enough width to read comfortably.

r0C.why: Identifiers stay intact and the table scans clearly, though extra width in the short-data columns leaves the note more tightly wrapped than in D.

ref_equal.why: The narrow Notes column turns one entry into a very tall, fragmented block, separating the surrounding server rows and making the table hard to scan.

r0B.why: The note has room to read, but every zone identifier wraps, making routine rows taller and slowing comparison across servers.

r0A.why: Host and zone identifiers stay intact, the compact fields are easy to compare, and Notes has enough width to keep the exceptional row reasonably short.

r0C.why: Identifiers stay intact and the columns read clearly, though the extra space in the short fields leaves Notes narrower and its row taller than in C.

ref_auto.why: Zone identifiers wrap over three lines and some host names split, disrupting nearly every row despite the generous Notes width.

raw.unsure: The images are small, so subtle differences in spacing are harder to judge.

provenance.note: AI visual design judgement; not a human reading study
